title: Don't Blame The Preferences: Examining The Emergence of Sycophancy in LLM Training
abstract: arXiv:2611.10045v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: AI sycophancy, the tendency of large language models (LLMs) to flatter users and affirm their beliefs, can undermine accuracy and contribute to misinformation, dependence, and overconfidence. Although prior work has benchmarked sycophancy in released models and proposed mitigations, its origins during training remain poorly understood. Preference alignment methods such as RLHF and DPO are often blamed, but their effects are rarely compared with earlier training stages. We investigate sycophancy across the training pipelines of three model families and three benchmarks. We find that sycophancy is largely established by the end of supervised fine-tuning (SFT), rather than introduced by preference alignment. Across all nine model benchmark combinations, SFT checkpoints attain at least 92% of preference aligned models' sycophancy scores and at least 85% of final models' scores; on average, they are about as sycophantic as final models. translated_title: 不要归咎于偏好：探究大语言模型训练中谄媚行为的产生
translated_abstract: AI谄媚行为，即大型语言模型（LLM）奉承用户并认同其信念的倾向，可能会损害准确性，并导致错误信息、依赖性和过度自信等问题。尽管先前的工作已经对已发布模型中的谄媚行为进行了基准测试并提出了缓解措施，但其在训练过程中的起源仍然知之甚少。诸如RLHF和DPO等偏好对齐方法经常被指责，但它们的效果很少与更早期的训练阶段进行比较。我们研究了三个模型系列和三个基准测试的训练流程中的谄媚行为。我们发现，谄媚行为主要在监督微调（SFT）结束时就已经确立，而不是由偏好对齐引入的。在所有九个模型-基准测试组合中，SFT检查点达到了偏好对齐模型谄媚分数的至少92%和最终模型分数的至少85%；平均而言，它们与最终模型的谄媚程度大致相当。
tldr: 研究发现LLM的谄媚行为主要在监督微调（SFT）阶段就已基本形成，而非由RLHF和DPO等偏好对齐方法引入，因此不应将谄媚问题归咎于偏好对齐。
en_tdlr: This study finds that LLM sycophancy is largely established by the end of supervised fine-tuning (SFT), rather than introduced by preference alignment methods like RLHF and DPO, suggesting preferences should not be blamed.
